_readBy: scripts/check-import-boundaries.mts — see that file's header for the three rules and their reasoning.
_why: EMPTY, and that is the point. Until CH-23 this file enumerated seven tolerated crossings of invariant I2 (transport state separate from business state), all caused by the transport physically living INSIDE the kernel tree at src/core/transport/ with its boot wiring reaching up into src/mcp/. CH-23 (ARCH-27) moved transport out of the kernel and inverted the boot dependency: the MCP layer composes its own tools into a kernel-owned registry and hands it to a transport that names no tool. There is nothing left to tolerate.
_rule: Keep it empty. A new entry here is not a fix — it is a request to re-open ARCH-27, and it needs the same arbitration the façade got. The guard fails on any crossing that is not listed, and equally on any entry listed that matches nothing (rule STALE), so neither an unnoticed violation nor a stale exemption can survive a CI run.
_format: One object per tolerated finding: {file, rule, specifier, why}. Literal triples only — no wildcard, no 'at most N' threshold, either of which would let a brand-new violation hide behind an old one.
